title: Dispatch: clear the exposed /^-+|-+$/ ReDoS sink in normalizeAbilityName (attempt 2)
description:
Dispatch bead for `eshyra-e1kt` (read that bead for the spec). Attempt 2 —
follow-up to `eshyra-e1kt.1`, which is correct and stays merged. This is an
ADDITIONAL fix, not a repair of that work.

Branch/worktree: `eshyra-e1kt.2`, cut from branch `eshyra-e1kt` (head c2f4e07,
which already contains the attempt-1 merge).
Model config: gpt-5.6-luna, reasoning effort medium.

## What happened

PR #523 (branch `eshyra-e1kt`) cleared alerts #15/#16/#17 as designed, but the
CodeQL check on the PR is FAILURE because a NEW alert appeared:

  #20  js/polynomial-redos  packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts:262
       "may run slow on strings with many repetitions of '-'"

That is the `.replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')` at the end of `normalizeAbilityName`.
The attempt-1 spec explicitly told the child NOT to touch it, on the reasoning
that the preceding `.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')` collapses every run of
non-alphanumerics — `-` included, since `-` is itself outside `[a-z0-9]` — to a
single `-`, so `-+` can never span more than one character. That reasoning is
correct about RUNTIME behavior and remains true. It is simply not something
CodeQL models.

Why it surfaced only now, confirmed against the API: on `refs/heads/main` the
open-alert set is exactly the three original sites and has never included
line 262, and the byte-identical `/^-+|-+$/g` at
`packages/core/src/state/attunement.ts:442` and
`packages/cli/src/characterDraftStore.ts:51` is not flagged either. The query
reports one sink per tainted source→sink flow; `\([^)]*\)` was the reported
sink on this chain, and removing it exposed the next sink on the SAME flow.
So this is not a regression introduced by attempt 1 and not a new code defect —
it is the rest of the same alert, and the owning bead's goal is to clear the
alerts.

## Scope

1. Rename `packages/core/src/state/parentheticalNames.ts` to
   `packages/core/src/state/nameNormalization.ts`. The module is about to
   cover more than parentheticals and the old name would be a lie. Update the
   two importers (`usageCounters.ts`, `actionEconomy.ts`), the export block in
   `packages/core/src/internal.ts`, and rename
   `packages/core/test/parentheticalNames.test.ts` to
   `packages/core/test/nameNormalization.test.ts`. Use `git mv` so the rename
   is recorded. Do not otherwise change the two existing helpers or their
   existing tests.

2. Add a third exported helper to that module:

   ```ts
   /**
    * Trim leading and trailing runs of `ch` without the polynomial
    * backtracking reported by CodeQL's js/polynomial-redos rule. Exactly
    * equivalent to `text.replace(/^<ch>+|<ch>+$/g, '')` for a single
    * non-special character.
    */
   export function trimEdgeChar(text: string, ch: string): string {
     let start = 0;
     let end = text.length;
     while (start < end && text[start] === ch) start += 1;
     while (end > start && text[end - 1] === ch) end -= 1;
     return text.slice(start, end);
   }
   ```

   Note this is equivalent UNCONDITIONALLY — it does not depend on the
   collapse invariant described above, which is the point: the invariant stays
   true but the code no longer silently relies on it.

3. Use it at `packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts:262`, so
   `normalizeAbilityName` ends `trimEdgeChar(…, '-')` instead of
   `.replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')`.

## Tests

Extend the renamed `nameNormalization.test.ts`:

- Add `trimEdgeChar` to the differential test, asserted against the original
  `/^-+|-+$/g` over fixtures that include `''`, `'-'`, `'--'`, `'-a-'`,
  `'---abc---'`, `'a-b'`, `'abc'`, and `'-'.repeat(9)`. Keep the original
  regex inline as the oracle, as the existing test does.
- Add a linearity test: `'-'.repeat(200_000)` returns `''` inside the same
  loose 1s wall-clock budget the existing long-input tests use.

Do not weaken or delete any existing assertion.

## Guard against a third round of whack-a-mole

Before committing, walk the remaining regexes reachable from `name` in
`normalizeAbilityName` and from `input.legendaryActionName` in
`normalizeLegendaryName` and confirm none is polynomial: `[^a-z0-9]+` in a
global replace is a single non-ambiguous repetition with no overlapping
prefix, `.toLowerCase()` and `.trim()` use no regex, and the helpers in this
module are regex-free. Record that check in your completion notes. If you find
another genuinely ambiguous quantifier on those chains, fix it in the same
linear style rather than leaving it for another round.

## Out of scope

- `packages/core/src/state/attunement.ts:442` and
  `packages/cli/src/characterDraftStore.ts:51`. They carry the identical
  pattern but are NOT flagged on any ref — their inputs are not tainted by a
  library-input source. Leave them; do not "harden" them opportunistically.
- No usage-counter or action-economy semantics change; counter keys and
  display names stay byte-identical for every real input.
- No CodeQL configuration, ruleset, or alert-dismissal changes.

From the worktree root: `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing (it
rewrites files). All non-skipped tests must pass; documented skips are the
